title: Filtered lift of an invariant open--closed correspondence
statement:
Fix $A=A_{E,n}$ and separated finite-type $k$-schemes as in [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], an admissible correspondence $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_kX$ of [def-trf-correspondence], a closed reduced subscheme $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and its open complement $j:U\hookrightarrow X$. Assume $c_2(c_1^{-1}Z)\subseteq Z$ set-theoretically. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and $u:c_2^*K\to c_1^!K$, with exceptional adjoint $\widehat u:Rc_{1!}c_2^*K\to K$. Set $K_U=j_!j^*K$ and $K_Z=Ri_*i^*K$. A bounded filtered derived object means a complex of $A$-module sheaves with a finite decreasing filtration by subcomplexes, localized at maps inducing quasi-isomorphisms on all graded complexes. Write $\omega$ for forgetting the filtration and $\operatorname{gr}^r$ for the associated graded complex. Require the underlying object and all graded pieces to be in $D^b_{ctf}$; the filtered six operations are the classical derived lifts on this localization. The canonical localization filtration $\widetilde K$ is the two-step filtered object represented by any bounded sheaf complex $B^\bullet$ representing $K$ with $F^0B=B$, $F^1B=j_!j^*B$, $F^2B=0$, so $\omega\widetilde K=K$, $\operatorname{gr}^0\widetilde K=K_Z$ and $\operatorname{gr}^1\widetilde K=K_U$. The forgetful map
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{DF(X,A)}(Rc_{1!}c_2^*\widetilde K,\widetilde K)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X,A)}(Rc_{1!}c_2^*K,K)$$
is bijective. Its unique lift of $\widehat u$ has graded morphisms equal to the exceptional adjoints of $[i]_!(u|_Z)$ and $[j]_!(u|_U)$.

Here $c|_Z:c_1^{-1}(Z)_{\mathrm{red}}\to Z\times Z$ and $c|_U:c^{-1}(U\times U)\to U\times U$ are the induced correspondences. Their coefficient maps are obtained by ordinary pullback of $\widehat u$ and the compact-support base-change maps, followed by exceptional adjunction. Their extensions are the proper closed pushforward of [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward] for $i$, and the extension by zero for $j$ using the invariant inclusion $c_2^{-1}(U)\subseteq c_1^{-1}(U)$.

The filtered construction is on the small etale sites, with its finite filtered bounded-constructible objects and operations transported to the small pro-etale categories by the exact comparison of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. All displayed trace classes are read in the coefficient categories of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions].

source.place: §5.2.3 and §5.3.3 (the bijection of filtered and unfiltered Hom sets and identification of graded maps); restriction construction §1.5.6

proof.text: Work on the small etale site. The constructible-origin equivalence [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], the fully faithful comparison [sk-prop-sf-comparison], and [det-ctf-finite-comparison-localizing] identify the etale and stipulated pro-etale Hom groups and operations used below. The degreewise short exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact], exact inverse images [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], exact extension by zero [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], and exact closed direct image [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] verify every hypothesis of [lem-trf-localization-filtration-descent], so $B\mapsto(B,F^1B=j_!j^*B)$ descends canonically, with grades $K_Z=i_*i^*K$ in degree $0$ and $K_U=j_!j^*K$ in degree $1$. The finite-stage preservation statements [prop-functor-package] put these objects in $D^b_{ctf}$. Denote the localization arrows by $a:K_U\to K$ and $b:K\to K_Z$.

source.place: Example 5.2.3, finite-coefficient construction; etale/pro-etale reading as stipulated in the item

proof.text:
Put $T=Rc_{1!}c_2^*$. Let $V=c_2^{-1}(U)$ with open inclusion $h:V\hookrightarrow C$. If $v\in V$ lay in $c_1^{-1}(Z)$, invariance would imply $c_2(v)\in Z$, a contradiction. Thus $V\subseteq c_1^{-1}(U)$, $V=c^{-1}(U\times U)$, and $c_1h=jp_1$, $c_2h=jp_2$ define the legs $p_1,p_2:V\to U$ of $c|_U$. Base change for extension by zero [sbc-prop-extension-by-zero-and-arbitrary-base-change] gives $c_2^*K_U\simeq h_!p_2^*j^*K$. Compact-support composition [prop-functor-package] therefore gives
$$TK_U\simeq Rc_{1!}h_!p_2^*j^*K\simeq j_!M_U,\qquad M_U=Rp_{1!}p_2^*j^*K.$$
Applying the same extension-by-zero base change to the disjoint square $Z\times_XU=\varnothing$ gives $i^*j_!=0$, hence $i^*TK_U=0$. The open self-base-change square gives $j^*j_!\simeq\mathrm{id}$. These comparisons use the actual units and counits of the compact-support functors, not just an assertion about support.

source.place: §5.3.3, equation (5.2), after interchanging the two legs; §1.5.9

proof.text:
For every cochain shift $q\in\mathbf Z$, ordinary derived adjunction [fix-prop-adjunctions] gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X,A)}(TK_U,K_Z[q])\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Z,A)}(i^*TK_U,i^*K[q])=0.$$
The etale module-sheaf category has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. By the ordinary global-Hom interpretation in [lem-trf-filtered-derived-hom-calculus], all cohomology groups of $R\operatorname{Hom}_X(TK_U,K_Z)$ vanish, so that complex is zero in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$ (the Hom groups being compared between the etale and pro-etale sides by the identification of Step 1). This is vanishing in every cochain degree, rather than just vanishing of the degree-zero Hom group.

For the separated finite-type legs choose compactifications by [thm-nagata-compactification]: their targets are quasi-compact (finite type over a field) and quasi-separated (separated over a field). These are supplied compactifications in the sense of the filtered-operation lemma. The filtered lifts of [lem-trf-filtered-derived-operation-lifts] commute with forgetting the filtration and with each graded functor; this applies to $T$ by its compactification-derived realization and to the localization arrows. Hence $P=T\widetilde K$ and $Q=\widetilde K$ have grades $P^0=TK_Z$, $P^1=TK_U$, $Q^0=K_Z$, $Q^1=K_U$, and no other grades. The etale module-sheaf category has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], so apply [lem-trf-filtered-derived-hom-calculus] to $H=R\operatorname{Hom}_F(P,Q)$. For negative filtration degrees its graded formula reads $\operatorname{gr}^{-1}H=R\operatorname{Hom}_X(TK_U,K_Z)=0$ and $\operatorname{gr}^rH=0$ for $r<-1$. Since the filtration is finite, successively applying its truncation triangles shows $t_{<0}H=0$: the successive cones are exactly these zero graded complexes, starting with the zero tail. The truncation triangle then makes $\omega t_{\ge0}H\to\omega H$ an isomorphism. Its $H^0$ is precisely the forgetful map on Hom sets, so that map is bijective; by the identification of Step 1 this is the forgetful map of the statement. (The filtered lifts used here are those of the general first clause of [lem-trf-filtered-derived-operation-lifts], applied to the etale module-sheaf categories.) In particular $\widehat u$ has a unique filtered lift $\widetilde u$.

Write $v_U=\operatorname{gr}^1\widetilde u:TK_U\to K_U$ and $v_Z=\operatorname{gr}^0\widetilde u:TK_Z\to K_Z$. Functoriality and uniqueness of the filtration truncation triangles in [lem-trf-filtered-derived-hom-calculus], together with the graded comparisons in [lem-trf-filtered-derived-operation-lifts], identify the image under $T$ of the localization triangle with the filtration truncation triangle. Since the first and third terms have only grades $1$ and $0$, respectively, this gives
$$a v_U=\widehat u\,T(a),\qquad v_ZT(b)=b\widehat u.$$
The open equation determines $v_U$ uniquely by Step 2 and $j_!\dashv j^*$: after $TK_U\simeq j_!M_U$, composition with $a$ identifies both Hom sets with $\operatorname{Hom}_U(M_U,j^*K)$. For the closed equation, put $W=C\times_{c_1,X}Z$ and $Y=W_{\mathrm{red}}$. The leg factorizations $d_1,d_2:Y\to Z$ and the natural comparison of [lem-trf-invariant-closed-basechange-identification] give $i^*T(a)=0$ and $i^*T(b)$ invertible; [fix-prop-adjunctions] then gives uniqueness by ordinary adjunction. Thus each equation determines its graded map uniquely.

source.place: §5.3.3, last paragraph; §1.5.6, with reduction invariance and ordinary adjunction made explicit

proof.text:
Let $\kappa:TK_U\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!M_U$ be Step 2's comparison and let $\lambda:M_U\to j^*TK$ be $j^*T(a)$ after $j^*\kappa^{-1}$. The exceptional adjoint of $u|_U$ is
$$r_U=j^*\widehat u\circ\lambda:M_U\to j^*K.$$
This is exactly restriction of the exceptional adjoint followed by compact-support base change, as prescribed in the statement. Extension by zero gives $w_U=j_!r_U\circ\kappa:TK_U\to K_U$. The equation $a w_U=\widehat uT(a)$ follows under $j_!\dashv j^*$: the restriction of its left side is $r_U$, and that of its right side is $j^*\widehat u\circ\lambda=r_U$, since $j^*a=\mathrm{id}$. The adjunction is a bijection on these Hom sets, so equality after this restriction is equality of the original maps. The unit, composition and extension-by-zero comparisons used here are those of [lem-trf-filtered-derived-operation-lifts] and [prop-functor-package]. Step 5 therefore gives $v_U=w_U$, the exceptional adjoint of $[j]_!(u|_U)$.

source.place: §§1.5.9 and 5.3.3, identification of the open graded map

proof.text:
Set $Y=W_{\mathrm{red}}$, with closed inclusion $h_Z:Y\hookrightarrow C$, and let $d_1,d_2:Y\to Z$ be the factorizations of the legs obtained in Step 5. Put $T_Z=Rd_{1!}d_2^*$ and $N=i^*K$. Compact-support base change, reduction invariance and the adjunction-coherent comparisons of [prop-functor-package], [i-topology] and [fix-prop-adjunctions] give $\theta:i^*TK\xrightarrow{\sim}T_ZN$. By definition the exceptional adjoint of the restricted coefficient map is $r_Z=i^*\widehat u\circ\theta^{-1}:T_ZN\to N$. Unfold the proper coefficient pushforward [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward] for $(i,h_Z)$: its ordinary half is the unit for $h_Z$ followed by $d_2^*$ of the counit $i^*i_*N\to N$, and its exceptional half is adjoint to the compact-support composition followed by the exceptional counit. Thus its exceptional adjoint on $K_Z=i_*N$ is $w_Z=i_*r_Z\circ\beta$, where
$$\beta:TK_Z=Rc_{1!}c_2^*i_*N\xrightarrow{Rc_{1!}\eta_{h_Z}}Rc_{1!}h_{Z*}h_Z^*c_2^*i_*N\simeq i_*Rd_{1!}d_2^*i^*i_*N\xrightarrow{i_*Rd_{1!}d_2^*\varepsilon_i}i_*T_ZN.$$
The closed immersions $i,h_Z$ are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], as required by that definition. The base-change mate formula and the ordinary triangle identity of [fix-prop-adjunctions] identify
$$\beta\,T(b)=i_*\theta\circ\eta_{i,TK}.$$
Indeed $h_Z^*c_2^*b=d_2^*i^*b$; composing with $d_2^*\varepsilon_{i,N}$ is the identity by the triangle identity for $i^*\dashv i_*$, and the remaining unit for $h_Z$ and composition comparison are exactly the base-change mate defining $\theta$. Therefore
$$w_ZT(b)=i_*r_Z\,i_*\theta\,\eta_{i,TK}=i_*i^*\widehat u\,\eta_{i,TK}=\eta_{i,K}\widehat u=b\widehat u,$$
where the last equality is naturality of the ordinary unit. Step 5 gives $v_Z=w_Z$. This proves the claimed identification with the exceptional adjoint of $[i]_!(u|_Z)$.

Exactness of etale extension by zero needed for descent of the canonical filtration; no specialized contracting theorem supplies it.
